questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Japan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Japan article.

questions.proof: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and its biggest city.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Japan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Japan article.

questions.proof: Honshu, which means 'Mainland' in the Japanese language, is the biggest island.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is a group of islands close to the east coast of Korea, China and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “China”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Japan article.

questions.proof: It is a group of islands close to the east coast of Korea, China and Russia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Senkaku Islands problem (with China and _____)”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “China”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Territorial problem” part of the Japan article.

questions.proof: Senkaku Islands problem (with China and Taiwan)

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “On 11 March _____, Japan suffered one of the largest earthquakes in its recorded history, triggering the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Japan article.

questions.proof: On 11 March 2011, Japan suffered one of the largest earthquakes in its recorded history, triggering the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster.
